parsed_payload.reasoning: Let \(\phi=\angle BAC\). Then \(\sin\phi=1/(5\sqrt2)\) and \(\sin(135^\circ-\phi)=4/5\). Correct Law of Sines gives \(a/\sin\phi=b/\sin(135^\circ-\phi)=c/\sin45^\circ=k\), so \(a=k/(5\sqrt2)\), \(b=4k/5\), \(c=k\sqrt2/2\). The perimeter condition gives \(k(1/(5\sqrt2)+4/5+\sqrt2/2)=24+18\sqrt2\). Since \(1/(5\sqrt2)+\sqrt2/2=3\sqrt2/5\), this is \(k(4+3\sqrt2)/5=24+18\sqrt2=6(4+3\sqrt2)\), so \(k=30\). Thus \(a=30/(5\sqrt2)=3\sqrt2\). The altitude from \(B\) to \(AC\) is \(h=a\sin45^\circ=3\sqrt2\cdot \sqrt2/2=3\). Final answer: \(3\).
